title: Reflection, refraction, mirrors, lenses and ray diagrams.

concepts.name: Laws of Reflection
concepts.real_life_application: A flat wall mirror flips your image because each light ray obeys the equal-angles rule — the same law engineers use to build car rear-view and make-up mirrors.
day_to_day_usage: Looking into any flat mirror while grooming
CCTV mirrors at ATM corners and blind turns
concepts.industry_relevance: Periscopes in submarines, laser alignment in metro tunnels, retro-reflectors on road signs.
concepts.engineering_domains: Aerospace & Satellites, Optics / LASIK & Lenses, Electrical & Power Grids, Robotics & EVs
concepts.future_careers: Engineer (Space/Mech/Electrical), Data Scientist, Medical Physicist, Defence Scientist

concepts.name: Refraction and Snell's Law
concepts.real_life_application: A straw in a glass of water looks bent and a swimming pool looks shallower — light changes speed when it crosses air into water.
day_to_day_usage: Bent straw in a cold-drink glass
Pool appearing shallower than it is
Rainbow after rain (light bends in raindrops)
concepts.industry_relevance: Camera lenses, spectacles and contact lenses, optical fibres.
concepts.engineering_domains: Aerospace & Satellites, Optics / LASIK & Lenses, Electrical & Power Grids, Robotics & EVs
concepts.future_careers: Engineer (Space/Mech/Electrical), Data Scientist, Medical Physicist, Defence Scientist

exercises.question: A concave mirror forms a real image at infinity. Where is the object placed?
exercises.solution: When the object is at the focal point of a concave mirror, the reflected rays become parallel and the image forms at infinity.
